reuse.why: Changes the existing shared applyWeekendRule in shared/schedules.ts and feeds it the schedule frequency, so all three existing callers pick up the new rule; schedule-template wraps it in two local helpers rather than a shared one.

duplication.why: The 'skip null occurrences with a lookahead window' idea is written twice with different constants (WEEKDAY_LOOKAHEAD in getNextDate, take: count * 7 plus filter/slice in getUpcomingDates), and schedule-template keeps its two identical skipWeekend ternaries while calling applyWeekendRule twice per iteration.

placement.why: The weekend decision stays in the shared schedules module where it already lived; the null-handling helpers in budget/schedule-template.ts are local to the one caller, which is acceptable but means each caller interprets 'skipped' itself.

scope.why: Only the weekend rule, its callers, the frequency passed through parseRecurDate, and tests.

maintainability.why: Turning applyWeekendRule's return into Date | null pushes skip handling and an ad-hoc lookahead onto every caller, and getAdjustedOccurrence's '?? date' fallback silently returns the weekend date for skipped occurrences, which a maintainer has to reason about.

bypasses_abstraction.where: All callers still go through applyWeekendRule.

disguised_duplication.where: The lookahead-and-skip loop over occurrences in getNextDate (shared/schedules.ts, WEEKDAY_LOOKAHEAD) is re-done in getUpcomingDates (server/schedules/app.ts) as take: count * 7 + filter + slice instead of sharing one function.

one_place.where: The daily-skip rule itself is decided in applyWeekendRule (packages/loot-core/src/shared/schedules.ts), which getNextDate, getUpcomingDates and createScheduleList all call; only the handling of the skipped (null) result is per caller.
